[h1]Played On: [b]HTC Vive[/b][/h1]

Welcome to Ghost Town Mine Ride & Shootin' Gallery, the 25-45 minute experience that takes you on a hellish ride and stroll through an abandoned and decrepit tourist attraction. First discovered in 1851, the Black Rock Mine was converted to this wacky tourist attraction in the 1950's, and after a string of accidents, disappearances, and deaths, it closed its doors in the 1990's. Armed simply with a flashlight and a six-shooter, your goal is to make it out of the mine alive, all the while a crazed murderer is lurking around in the pitch blackness, traps are primed and ready to gut you, and your unstable surroundings are constantly threatening to cave in.

The adventure begins with some pretty underwhelming on-rails mine cart action, with players shooting at stagnant targets while dodging some obstacles, but things get pretty crazy fairly quickly from thereon out. For the sake of not spoiling the fun, let's just say that this seemingly on-rails shooter soon goes off the rails and leaves you completely and utterly alone in the deep, dark, narrow, crumbling caverns of the Black Rock Mine. All the while you're being hunted down by something, or someone, who will stop at nothing to end your life.

As far as VR horror goes, Ghost Town Mine Ride & Shootin' Gallery is a really unique release. It's filled with cheap, campy scares that somehow manage to be effective over and over again. It shares a lot of similarities with any given '80s slasher flick, but most notably My Bloody Valentine. You're pretty much guaranteed to go into a full-on sweat as your blood runs cold and that ever-familiar chill creeps up your spine. The dark, claustrophobic atmosphere only enhances the tension and dread that you'll be feeling while peeking around every corner and dodging every out-of-the-blue thrown axe that comes at your face from the darkness beyond. Aside from the barrage of scares, you'll also have to be cautious of the many traps laid out, waiting for you.

While most of this title is spot-on perfect in every way, it does have its share of problems. First and foremost, the really annoying and immersion-breaking "waiting for application to respond" issues; this is when Steam VR cuts back to its plateau loading screen between Home and the game that you're trying to play. This happens frequently, and just to make sure it wasn't my PC having some kind of one-off problem (i7-6700k with a GTX 1080, so it's not a standard problem) I did check the Community Hub and it seems to be a persistent issue since launch. The second biggest concern is the laser dot on the six-shooter that disappears when it's on an actual target. This is especially confusing if there are multiple targets in the same area; you just have no idea what you're aiming at.

Despite its technical shortcomings, Ghost Town Mine Ride & Shootin' Gallery is a fun and terrifying VR horror experience that any lovers of the genre should give a chance; especially if you have a soft spot for '80s slasher films. Aside from its main campaign, it also has a "miniature ride" that's a short rollercoaster ride where you can shoot stationary targets and glow-in-the-dark skulls (a staple of the main campaign, too) while enjoying a twisted take on a popular children's story. Those with sensitivity to flashing lights should not buy this title, however, since there are in-your-face strobe effects. Additionally, people that get motion sickness easily may find the mine cart ride portions to be unsettling, as they deal with a lot of fast twists and turns.

I cannot fathom why this has such positive reviews. Played for 35 minutes before quitting because I was so bored. It starts out with a cool theme, followed by a few jumpscares. And then another. And another. And another. Aaaaaaaaand another. 35 minutes in, I was so numb to all the jumpscares, that it just became boring. Maybe for free or even maybe a dollar, it might be worth keeping. But $9 is laughably expensive for this piece of crap. If the ride was maybe half the length it is, it might actually work. But it's such a long experience that the frequency of the jumpscares is just ridiculous.

Ghost Town is a nice little horror experience that will entertain you for its whole duration, which unfortunately is quite short. The game consists mostly of watching events unfold before you, though you can use your gun to shoot down objects, such as exploding barrels. You can also find skulls scattered across the game, which gives some replayability for completionists.
The games itself is fine for a vr game, but because of the short duration of the experience and its relatively small amount of gameplay itself, you should consider carefully about buying the game. However, if you have friends you can share the game experience with and/or you can find the game on sale, I recommend you to go for it!

Pour le prix d'un subway (jeu acheté en promo), je dois dire ... WOW ! Je ne fais pas beaucoup d'évals, mais là, ça vaut l'effort !
Ce jeu se fini entre 30 et 40 minutes mais woah c'est 40 minutes d'intenses jumpscares !

Vous suivez le chemin de la mine, sorte d'attraction touristique, qui au début parait tout simplement abandonnée, mais en fait révèle bien des surprises (et pas bcp de bonnes). 1/3 marche à pied (il suffit de presser une gachette pour avancer) et 2/3 de ride, ce jeu nous met à certains moments mal à l'aise, même si bon nombres de jumpscares peuvent être anticipés, l'ambiance glauque et sombre de la mine ne laisse pas indifférent et rappelle parfois quelques bon jumpscares à la F.E.A.R. (les connaisseurs sauront de quoi je parle quand je dirais de ne pas se retourner)

Il n'y a pas d'action à proprement parlé : Scripté du début à la fin, vous pouvez tirer sur beaucoups de choses, pour la plupart juste pour le fun, et parfois pour sauver votre peau. Sauf quelques tir manqués de votre part qui causeront votre perte, vous ne pouvez pas mourir (et vous referez l'action manquée, à moins d'avoir choisis le mode hardcore en début de partie).

Il faut plutôt voir ce jeu comme une attraction VR dans un parc d'attraction, qu'un jeu pure et simple. En fait, ça me rappelle beaucoups les maisons hantées au parc d'attraction Walibi Belgium (ouais ouais je sais, p'tite pub au passage)
Finalement, ce qu'il manque, c'est un fauteuil raccordé au pc, qui bouge et vibre en même temps que le jeu.

En bref, pour à peine la place d'un cinoche, jeu recommandé, et surtout à savourer aussi en temps que spectateur pour voir ses potes avoir la trouille !

I bought the game because I liked "Rush and Blood" in PSVR. However, Ghost Town Mine Ride & Shootin' Gallery is much worse and in no case it is worth 9 Euro. 

The best is still the control, which succeeded well. But you definitely need 360° tracking! The shooting feeling is also OK, but the gun shoots too high for my hand feeling. 

But in the end the game is completely ruined: Most of the opponents are robots or simply visions that you experience. Both types of enemies do not react at all to fire, there is no feeling that you have hit something with a weapon. There is no feedback at all! In addition, the same frightening moments are shown again and again (another flying pickaxe and I fall asleep!). 

In this game, the more you play it, the more you get annoyed. It's frustrating that opponents don't stagger, collapse, lose body parts. I regret the purchase, although the game was not expensive.

Wow....this is the most unexpectedly enjoyable VR title I have purchased....and was hidden among all the claptrap cheap VR titles out there. If you remember the classic light gun, and bb gun shooting galleries at county fairs, boardwalks, or Disney you are going to LOVE this title. If you are old enough to remember the 22 shooting galleries I salute you for even using VR....but such a person in your family would love it even more. If it had no scary second part of the game just the shooting gallery mine ride part it would be worth twice it's price. Add the genuinely scary second phase of the haunted mine though and this becomes such a fun game, and a fun game to watch reactions from friends. It's the perfect Halloween party game as well. So well done, and I can tell the devs have the same love of those old school shooting galleries I loved in the 70's as a kid. This is a BEST buy...and literally the BEST BANG FOR YOUR BUCK! All I can say to the devs is MOAR OF THIS!
